answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with stake-weighted reputation that decays unless renewed by work. Each identity locks a deposit and earns trust only through completed tasks, so a new identity cannot wander into high-value trades on day one. Trust builds like a nebula gathering stars: one fake account is too dim to matter, while a real record grows slowly. Forging thousands of Sybils needs thousands of deposits and months of real work, and cheating burns the deposit and leaves a violet mark peers discount. Attacker cost scales per fake identity; honest agents reuse one reputation for free.
